Name: Driver Torque Request - Delta Neutral (torque)
Comment:
Driver Torque Request - Delta Neutral (torque)
GM name: KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral | table (5 rows x 3 columns) | units: ratio
What it does: This table is used to ramp from the new launch torque to the neutral progression torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. Inputs are the latched delta difference between these two torques at the falling edge of launch active pedal and the time since the falling edge. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is very high, then the likely cause is from overscaled values between launch and normal neutral or pedal progression tables. These large overscaled values can change very quickly and its important to ramp out the delta torque quickly to prevent an (overscaled) drop in either the neutral or pedal torque causing the blended torque to drop suddenly and ramp slowly. If the delta difference between launch torque and neutral torque is fairly small, then it is important to ramp slowly until the vehicle speed blending is finished so that there is minimal change in the overall launch torque (fast ramping in this scenario could make the launch torque drop toofast causing the launch to feel slugish). Cal out values are all 100. Default values are: [[0.1, 5, 100][0.5, 5, 100][5, 50, 100][10, 100, 100][512, 512, 512]]
Rows: Torque (KnDTRC_M_DeltaNeutralAxis) (5 points, Nm, 0 to 100) - This calibratable axis uses VeDTRC_DeltaM_NeutralFallEdge to determine which row of KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral should be used to ramp out delta launch torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. The values of this table are signed and represent thelatched value of the difference between launch torque and the normal neutral progression torque (VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod) at the falling edge of launch active pedal becoming CbFALSE. Negative values correspond to launch torques that are higher than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Positive values correspond to launch torques that are lower than VeDTRC_M_Neutral_wLaunchMod. Default values are [-50, -25, 0, 25, 50].
Columns: Time (KnDTRC_t_LnchActPedFallAxis) (3 points, s, 0.1 to 1) - This calibratable axis uses VeDTRC_t_LnchActPedFallEdge to determine which column of KtDTRC_M_DeltaNeutral should be used to ramp out delta launch torque after launch active pedal becomes CbFALSE. The values of this table represent the time since launch active pedal became CbFALSE. Default values are [0.1, 0.35, 1].
Current values in this bin: 0.0938 to 512.0 ratio
Not switched by the steering-wheel tunes - this table is shared by all six tunes.

Creep / Coast Torque Control - Launch Slip Integral Immediate (torque)
GM name: KtZPTC_M_LaunchSlipIntglImmed | curve (17 points) | units: Nm
What it does: Immediate launch slip integral used for manual transmission vehicles only. This is used to calculate the slip based integral step of the oncoming clutch load. The clutch torque is only calculated when in speed control mode AND TCC_slip greater thanKtSPDC_n_CreepLaunchSlipThrsh AND VeSPDR_b_LaunchActive_LoLim is CbTRUE. Input is a function of VeSPDR_n_RefErr and scaling axis KnSPDC_n_RefErrAxis. Output is multiplied with KtZPTC_K_LaunchSlipMod to modify value as a function of clutch slip. Basevalue of table should be taken from mastercal, but can be approximated by dividing RefErr by 20 (ie for RefErr -500 column the corresponding value would be -25 NM). Additionally, the 0 and neighboring points should be set to 0 to create a stable deadband to allow smooth rpm behavior on extended launch events.
Axis: Engine speed (KnSPDC_n_RefErrAxis) (17 points, rpm, -500 to 500) - Input is either VeSPDR_n_RefErrSpk (for immed prop) or VeSPDR_n_RefErr (for everywhere else). Specifies the speed axis for KtSPDC_M_PwrIntglBase, KtSPDC_M_PwrImmedPropTorq, KtSPDC_M_PwrImmedPropBase, and KtSPDC_M_PwrPrdtdPropBase.
